challenges.name: status-codes-quiz
challenges.title: What does this status tell the client?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the status audit: a learner probing draft course ids, and the queued submission that the mobile app showed as "0 of 0 tests passed".

questions.explanation: True. 403 means "I know who you are and you may not access this resource", which confirms the resource exists; 404 means there is nothing there for this caller. Trying ids and keeping the 403s lists every draft, which is how the forum thread found upcoming courses. RFC 9110 lets a server that wants to hide a forbidden resource answer 404 instead, and the hidden and the missing answer must then be identical, body and headers included. The misconception is that 403 is always the "more correct" answer for a resource the caller may not see: it is correct only when the caller is allowed to know the resource exists.

questions.question:
After the fix, the API answers:

POST /submissions
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Location: /submissions/sub_88

{"id":"sub_88","status":"queued"}

A reviewer proposes going back to 200 OK with the same headers and body, to avoid changing the mobile app's status handling.

Statement: "For clients the two answers are equivalent: both are 2xx success codes, and the body already says the submission is queued."
questions.explanation: False. A 200 to a POST says the processing is finished and the body is its result, which is exactly what mobile app 3.6 assumed when it rendered "0 of 0 tests passed". 202 says the request was accepted but not completed and may still fail, and its Location points to the status resource to poll. Clients, generated SDKs, retry policies and dashboards branch on the status line; they do not search the body for a word like "queued". The misconception is that every 2xx means the same thing; the status code is the client's next step, and the next step here is "wait and poll", not "show the result".

challenges.name: choose-status-code
challenges.title: Choose the status code and the headers
challenges.description: Every CodeDev API handler reports a business outcome, and one function turns the HTTP method and that outcome into the status code and the headers the client needs. Write chooseResponse(method, outcome) returning { status, headers } with exactly this table (outcome.kind -> status, headers): ok -> 204 when the method is DELETE, 200 otherwise, no headers; created -> 201, with Location: outcome.location only when the method is POST (a PUT that creates has no Location); accepted -> 202 with Location: outcome.location (the status resource to poll); already_exists -> 200; validation_failed -> 400; rule_violated -> 422; unauthenticated -> 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="codedev"; forbidden -> 403, or 404 when outcome.hidden is true (the caller may not learn that the resource exists); not_found -> 404; version_conflict -> 409; payment_required -> 402; rate_limited -> 429 with Retry-After; gone -> 410; dependency_down -> 503 with Retry-After; method_not_allowed -> 405 with Allow; any other kind (kinds are case-sensitive) -> 500 with no headers. Rules: compare the method case-insensitively ("delete" is DELETE). Retry-After is outcome.retryAfterSeconds written as a string when it is a number that is a whole number >= 0, otherwise "60". Allow lists outcome.allowed uppercased, without duplicates, in the order GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, joined with ", "; methods not in that list are dropped, and a missing or empty list gives Allow: "". A created outcome for a POST, or any accepted outcome, without a non-empty location string is a handler bug: 500 with no headers. Header names are exactly Location, Retry-After, Allow and WWW-Authenticate; a response without headers has headers {}. The test runner reads { cases: [{ method, outcome }] } as JSON and prints the list of { status, headers }.
hints: For each outcome, ask what the client must do next and which header it needs to do it: where is the new resource, how long should it wait, which methods may it use, how does it sign in? Which outcomes also depend on the HTTP method?

Look at the four places where the table is not one fixed status: ok (DELETE), created (POST only gets Location), forbidden (hidden), and the three header values that are computed - Retry-After from a value that may be missing or not a whole number, Allow from a list that may be in any order and case, and Location that may be missing.

A similar table for the CodeDev web app's cache: kind "fresh" -> 200; "stale" -> 200 with an Age header only for GET; "moved" -> 308 with Location; anything else -> 500. For ("get", { kind: "stale" }) you uppercase the method first and return 200 with the header; for ("POST", { kind: "moved" }) without a location you return 500 with headers {}. A list ["b", "A", "a"] in the fixed order A, B, C becomes "A, B" after uppercasing, removing duplicates and filtering the fixed order by what is present.

tests.name: The incident: a queued submission, a created course, a draft hidden from a learner
Client errors and the headers they need: 400, 422, 401, 402, 409, 404, 410, 429, 503, 405
The method matters: DELETE gets 204, a PUT that creates has no Location, repeats are 200
Retry-After: whole seconds kept (including 0), anything else becomes the default 60
Allow: uppercased, no duplicates, fixed order, unknown methods dropped, empty when none

headers.Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE

tests.name: Handler bugs are 500: unknown outcome, created by POST or accepted without a location
Large input: 1200 mixed outcomes and methods from a day of access logs
